documents.title: Loan Manager: loans payable and receivable
documents.content: The Loan Manager lists the money your business owes, under Loans Payable, and the money others owe it, under Loans Receivable, each with the original amount, the outstanding balance, the interest rate and the monthly payment, and a total of the balances to the cent. A loan needs who it is with, an original amount above zero, an outstanding balance from zero up to the original amount, and a real start date. The interest rate must be between 0 and 100 percent, the term a whole number of months, and the monthly payment cannot be negative. Amounts are saved to the cent. A new loan is saved against your workspace, so it appears in the list and in the Financial Snapshot; before this was fixed a newly added loan was saved without that and was never listed. The Save button is disabled while saving so one click adds one loan. The outstanding balance starts as the amount you enter, and each payment you record from the Record Payment item lowers it by that payment's principal; you can still correct it by hand by editing the loan.

documents.title: Owner equity, the Financial Snapshot and the loan application
documents.content: The Financial Snapshot shows a balance sheet and a Profitability card. Assets are cash in bank accounts, the petty cash box, inventory at cost, accounts receivable (the balance still owed on each invoice), capital assets at their balance after CCA claims, and loans receivable. Liabilities are accounts payable, loans payable, credit cards owing and payroll remittances still due. Owner's Equity is assets less liabilities, so Total Liabilities and Equity always equals Total Assets and the sheet balances. Owner contributions and draws, recorded on the Equity page, are tracked separately and do not change that figure. The Profitability card covers this calendar year to date only, before sales tax, business entries only, using the same figures as the Income Statement; it used to add up every entry ever recorded. The Matchbook summary and the Loan Application read the same balance sheet, so their Total Assets, Total Liabilities and Owner's Equity match the Snapshot; the application used to print Owner's Equity as zero. Equity entries need a real date and an amount above zero. The balance sheet is a summary built from what is recorded in Ogeemo, and a note on the sheet says what it could not include, such as an account with no opening balance, so confirm anything you give a lender with your accountant.
